pr_title: feat(medusa): Allow regexp in CORS configuration

comments.body: The pattern accepts the `g` and `y` flags, so `new RegExp(m[2], m[3])` can return a stateful regexp. The `cors` middleware calls `regex.test(origin)` on the same RegExp object for every request. With `g` or `y`, `lastIndex` persists between calls. For example, `store_cors="/https:\/\/.*\.example\.com/g"` matches the first request, then the next test starts at `lastIndex` and fails. The result is that valid origins are rejected on every other request. Origin regexps should not keep state, so drop `g` and `y` from the allowed flags or strip them.

`str.split(",")` runs before regexp detection, so any regexp containing a comma is broken into pieces. Examples are a quantifier like `/^https:\/\/a{1,3}\.example\.com$/` and an alternation inside braces. Each piece then fails to parse as a regexp and is silently kept as a literal string. No error is raised and the origin is never matched, so the intended CORS rule quietly does nothing.
